title: Net Interest Margin and Spread Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/01 - Net Interest Margin and Spread Analysis.md
goal: Assess the profitability of the bank’s core lending and deposit-taking operations by examining how effectively it manages the difference between interest income and interest expense, relative to its interest-earning assets.
dataRequired: Interest income (for a specific period)
Interest expense (for the same period)
Average interest-earning assets (e.g., loans, investments)
Average interest-bearing liabilities (e.g., deposits, borrowed funds)
Breakdown of yields on different asset classes and cost of different liability classes (optional but helpful)
improve: Rebalance the deposit base to reduce reliance on high-cost liabilities.
Optimize asset pricing strategies to ensure loan yields reflect current market conditions and risk levels.
Explore interest rate hedging strategies to manage rate volatility.
Diversify asset portfolios to achieve a stable yield across different economic cycles.

title: Non-Interest Income Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/02 - Non-Interest Income Analysis.md
goal: Evaluate the significance of fees, commissions, and other non-interest revenue streams in a commercial bank’s overall income mix and profitability.
dataRequired: Total non-interest income (e.g., fees, commissions, service charges)
Breakdown of major non-interest income categories (e.g., transaction fees, FX fees, wealth management fees)
Total operating income (interest income + non-interest income)
Historical data for trend analysis (e.g., quarterly or annually)
Peer or industry benchmarks for comparison
improve: Expand fee-based product offerings (e.g., treasury management, FX services, wealth management).
Enhance cross-selling initiatives to existing clients to increase adoption of additional services.
Improve pricing strategies for key services based on value delivered and market benchmarks.
Explore partnerships or acquisitions in high-margin fee areas (e.g., payments, merchant acquiring) to diversify revenue sources.

title: Efficiency Ratio and Cost Transformation
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/03 - Efficiency Ratio and Cost Transformation.md
goal: Evaluate the bank’s operating efficiency by analyzing the relationship between expenses and revenue, identifying cost drivers, and developing strategies to optimize costs without compromising service quality.
dataRequired: Total operating expenses (OPEX)
Total operating income (interest income + non-interest income, or total net revenue)
Efficiency Ratio for prior periods
Peer bank or industry benchmark data
Detailed breakdown of cost structure (e.g., salaries, overhead, technology expenses)
improve: Streamline operational processes through automation and digital tools to minimize manual workloads.
Optimize workforce allocation and consider rationalizing the branch network where feasible.
Negotiate favorable vendor contracts and explore outsourcing or shared services for non-core activities.
Consolidate overlapping systems and reduce redundancies across business units.
Establish clear cost-management frameworks, accountability measures, and regular performance reviews.
B. Lending and Credit Management

formulas.output: Step 2: Calculate the Efficiency Ratio. Efficiency Ratio
formulas.source: Step 2: Calculate the Efficiency Ratio. Efficiency Ratio = (Total Operating Expenses / Total Operating Income) x 100 Step 3: Compare the Efficiency Ratio over time and against peers or industry benchmarks to determine whether the bank’s cost structure is improving or deteriorating.

sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/04 - Loan Portfolio Quality and Concentration Analysis.md

dataRequired: Total loan balances by segment (e.g., SME, corporate, commercial real estate)
Loan classifications (e.g., performing, past due, non-performing)
Delinquency rates and Non-Performing Loans (NPLs)
Loan loss reserves/provisions data
Industry/sector exposures and associated limits
Collateral details (optional but helpful for deeper risk assessment)
improve: Strengthen credit underwriting policies for high-risk or overexposed segments.
Diversify the loan portfolio to reduce dependence on any single industry or geography.
Implement rigorous portfolio monitoring and early warning systems to identify emerging credit risks.
Revisit loan pricing strategies to ensure adequate returns for higher-risk segments.
Review and adjust loan loss provisioning practices to remain aligned with evolving credit risk profiles.

title: Loan Origination and Underwriting Standards Review
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/05 - Loan Origination and Underwriting Standards Review.md
goal: Evaluate the effectiveness of the bank’s loan origination processes and underwriting policies to ensure prudent credit risk-taking, adherence to regulatory requirements, and alignment with the bank’s overall risk appetite.
dataRequired: Current underwriting policies and guidelines
Detailed workflow for loan origination, including documentation requirements and approval processes
Loan application records (including time to decision and approval rates)

Invest in data analytics and credit scoring tools to improve risk assessment accuracy.
Streamline the loan origination process through process automation and clear decision-making authorities.
Implement ongoing training programs to ensure underwriters are well-versed in updated policies and risk assessment techniques.
Conduct regular back-testing of credit scoring models and adjust as necessary to enhance predictive power.

title: Collateral Management and LTV Review
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/06 - Collateral Management and LTV Review.md
goal: Assess how effectively the bank manages collateral securing its loans to maintain acceptable risk levels through the monitoring of LTV ratios.

Independent valuation reports or appraisals
Outstanding loan balances and corresponding LTV values
Collateral revaluation frequency data
Historical data on collateral calls, margin calls, or shortfalls
Collateral coverage ratios (if available)

Develop contingency plans for rapidly calling additional collateral or restructuring loans when LTV ratios exceed acceptable risk limits.

formulas.output: Step 3: Calculate the Loan-to-Value ratio for each loan or segment. LTV
formulas.source: Step 3: Calculate the Loan-to-Value ratio for each loan or segment. LTV = (Outstanding Loan Balance / Collateral Value) x 100 Step 4: Identify loans or portfolios with high LTV ratios (e.g., above policy thresholds). Segment the loans by collateral type (e.g., real estate, machinery, receivables) to understand areas of greater risk exposure.

sourcePath: data/analysis-library/commercial-bank/07 - Industry Exposure and Concentration Analysis.md

Diversify the loan book by targeting industries with stable or counter-cyclical growth patterns.
Implement stress testing scenarios focusing on high-exposure sectors.
Regularly monitor macroeconomic indicators and industry trends to stay proactive in managing concentration risks.
Develop specialized expertise or industry-focused teams for better risk assessment and client selection.
